2 min read
Just now

--

Every developer has searched for an error on Google at 2 AM.
You copy the error message, open Stack Overflow, Reddit, GitHub Issues, or random blog posts, hoping someone has already solved it.
Sometimes you find the answer.
But most of the time, you don't learn how they arrived at that solution.
You only see the final fix.
---
The Missing Piece
Real software engineering isn't just about writing code.
It's about debugging production issues, chasing race conditions, analyzing logs, comparing commits, reading documentation, trying five different approaches that fail, and finally discovering the real root cause.
Unfortunately, these stories rarely get documented.
When developers solve difficult problems, the knowledge often stays inside a company or disappears in Slack messages and private notes.
That means thousands of developers end up solving the same problem again.
---
That's Why I Built Dev Solved
Dev Solvedhttps://www.devsolved.com
Dev Solved is a platform where developers share real engineering incidents, not just answers.
Instead of asking only:
«"What's the solution?"»
We ask:
- What happened?
- What did you investigate?
- What approaches failed?
- How much time did it take?
- What was the root cause?
- What finally fixed it?
- What lessons did you learn?
Every incident becomes a learning experience for thousands of other developers.
---
More Than a Blog Platform
Dev Solved isn't meant to replace Stack Overflow or GitHub.
They are amazing for getting quick answers.
Dev Solved focuses on something different:
The complete engineering journey behind solving real-world problems.
Imagine reading stories like:
- How we reduced an API response from 15 seconds to 300 ms.
- Why our production deployment crashed at midnight.
- The hidden memory leak that took three days to find.
- How a tiny configuration mistake caused thousands of failed requests.
- The database query that brought our application down.
These aren't tutorials.
They're real engineering experiences.
---
Learning From Failures
Some of the best lessons come from things that didn't work.
That's why Dev Solved encourages developers to share failed attempts, debugging strategies, architecture decisions, and lessons learned.
Sometimes knowing what doesn't work is just as valuable as knowing what does.
---
Building Together
Software engineering grows because developers share knowledge.
Open source changed how we build software.
I hope Dev Solved can help change how we share engineering experiences.
Whether you're a student fixing your first bug or a senior engineer solving production incidents, your experience could save someone else hours—or even days—of debugging.
---
The Vision
My goal is simple:
Create the world's largest collection of real software engineering problem-solving stories.
Not tutorials.
Not copied answers.
Real incidents.
Real debugging.
Real solutions.
If you've solved a difficult problem recently, I'd love for you to share your story on Dev Solved.
Because someone, somewhere, is probably facing the exact same problem today.
